AdapterFailure.description:
Per-adapter `list()` failure surfaced alongside the rows from the
adapters that succeeded. Mirrors
[`crate::AdapterListError`] but carries [`RuntimeKind`] typed so
the reconciler can reason about it without re-parsing the string.

AdapterListError.description:
One adapter's `list()` failure, recorded alongside the successful rows
from the other adapters so callers can render "docker is down, lxc has
12 containers" without losing either side.

message.description: Human-readable error message — the `Display` form of [`AdapterError`].

AgentCreateAction.description:
The `agent.create` action. Only `run` today; the discriminant keeps the
surface six-verb-uniform and leaves room for future create actions.

oneOf.description: One-shot agent execution.

configured.description: True iff a credential is currently stored for this provider.

identity.description: Masked identifier (masked API key, account login, etc.) when configured.

BackendStatus.description: One probed backend and the models it currently serves.

models.description: Model identifiers discovered on this backend right now.

reachable.description: Whether at least one usable (non-embedding) model was discovered.

url.description: Base URL probed (empty for the Anthropic API).

BackupArtifact.description:
A backup artifact produced by [`ServiceBackend::backup`], restorable via
[`ServiceBackend::restore`]. The path is on the deploy target's filesystem.

BackupDetailView.description:
Which facet `backup.detail` reports. `providers` = registered backup kinds +
instances; `targets` = registered target kinds, placement fit, locations.

system.description:
The system the failure happened on. Empty = this one. A fleet-wide run
that reported a failure without naming its host would be unactionable.

target.description: The target the failure occurred against (`<kind>/<name>`), if known.

BackupRecord.description:
A produced, listable backup — the unit a restore selects by date.

Carries the identity a caller needs to *list* a kind's backups and *pick one
by date*, which the `backup.*` tool surface returns. Timestamps are Unix
**milliseconds** ([[time-values-in-milliseconds]]).

checksum.description: Optional integrity checksum over the payload (provider-defined algorithm).

createdMs.description: When the backup completed, Unix milliseconds.

fileCount.description: Number of files captured in the payload.

id.description:
Stable, sortable id for this backup: the compact UTC stamp
(`YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`). Unique within a `(kind, instance)` and the value a
restore selects with. Sorting ids lexically sorts them chronologically.

instance.description: Instance within the kind. `default` when the kind is single-instance.

kind.description: The backup KIND / provider that produced it (`host`, `service`, `nfs`, …).

note.description: Free-form provider note (e.g. which strategy/paths were captured).

path.description: Absolute path to this backup's payload directory on the host that holds it.

system.description:
The system holding this backup. Empty = this one.

`path` is absolute "on the host that holds it", which is unusable
without knowing which host that is. A fleet-wide listing that omitted
this would show backups a restore could not be routed to — and the
operator must never have to name a host to find out.

BackupTargetRef.description:
A reference to a configured backup TARGET — the WHERE axis, orthogonal to the
provider KIND (the WHAT). A target is named by its `kind` (a target kind in
the target-provider registry) plus a `name` that disambiguates multiple
targets of the same kind. The target kind's plugin owns the target's typed
settings; this ref names the kind and instance, and the target provider
resolves it to concrete storage
([[orca-core-generic-plugins-expose-functionality]], [[no-kind-owned-by-plugin]]).

kind.description: Target KIND — the registry key (`local`, or a plugin's `nfs`/`s3`/…).

name.description: Instance name within the kind. `default` for the single, unnamed target.

BridgeReport.description: Outcome of a bridge reconcile pass.

cleared.description: Keys auto-dismissed because their finding cleared.

raised.description: Keys of notifications raised (created or reactivated) this pass.

CapabilityListOutput.description:
Read shape for `system.detail{view=capabilities}`: every provider this host
has ever probed or had set by an operator. Empty before the first daemon
startup probe runs.

CapabilityRow.description:
Flat, JsonSchema-friendly projection of [`HostCapability`]. `state`
is a string at the boundary so consumers (UI / scripts) can match on
the literal values without depending on an enum type, mirroring the
`runtime` field on `containers.unhold` / `containers.unwedge`.

detail.description: Version string when Available (e.g. docker server version).

lastProbed.description:
Unix epoch seconds when the row was last written. Advances on
probe, disable, and enable.

reason.description:
Failure reason (Absent) or operator-supplied note (Disabled).
`None` when Available.

CatalogEntry.description:
One first-party plugin known to orca. Installability is NOT read from
`status`: `plugin.install --name` is release-derived — it resolves the repo's
actual release asset for this target triple and succeeds iff the plugin has
published one, so a plugin declares itself installable by cutting a release.
`status` is descriptive metadata only (a coarse hint for `plugin.list`); it
no longer gates install and may lag the repo's real release state.

docsUrl.description: Where to read about the plugin.

name.description: Catalog name, e.g. `"jellyfin"`. Matches the plugin's `target_software`.

repoUrl.description: Public GitHub repo hosting the plugin's source + release pipeline.

status.description:
Descriptive hint only — **nothing gates on it**, not `plugin.install`
and not `plugin.update`. Installability is release-derived: the catalog
contract says publish a release, not hand-tune this field.

It is hand-maintained and therefore drifts. Measured 2026-09-27:
`agents` and `syncthing` each publish five releases while this field
still reads `"unreleased"`, so reading it as "has releases" is wrong in
practice as well as in principle.

This doc previously claimed `plugin.update` gated on it while the code
~1000 lines below said the opposite in as many words. That contradiction
was load-bearing: it is the premise that produced two withdrawn claims on
#648 (see #650). Keep this aligned with `plugin_update`, which is the
authority.

targetSoftware.description: External software the plugin integrates, e.g. `"jellyfin"`.

gaps.description:
Indices into `points` where a gap exists. `gaps[i] = N` means the
renderer should break the path between `points[N-1]` and `points[N]`.

lastValue.description:
Most recent raw value (pre-scaling). `None` when the series is empty
or every sample lacked this metric. Lets the client render a
"current value" label without re-fetching the raw history.

points.description: Pre-scaled SVG-space points, ordered oldest → newest.

vmax.description:
Y-axis ceiling used for scaling. Clamped to a floor of 1.0 to avoid
div-by-zero on flat-zero series.

xAxisLabels.description:
Evenly-spaced relative-time labels for the x axis (e.g.
`["-5m", "-3m", "-1m", "now"]`). Length 0 when the series has fewer
than 2 points.

ClaimEndpoint.description:
A network endpoint a claimed workload listens on. Enables service-identity
correlation: a runtime [`crate::service_identity::ServiceRegistration`] keyed
by `(host, port)` joins to the claim whose `endpoints` contain that port on a
matching host.

publishedPort.description:
Host-published port when the runtime maps one (docker `-p`). `None` = not
published to the host (reachable only on the workload's own address).

ClaimNode.description: A non-peer entity synthesized from a host's [`contract::TopologyClaim`].

children.description:
Container claims nested under a synthesized `stack` node. Empty on leaf
(container/vm/lxc) nodes; populated only on `kind == "stack"` nodes,
which group the container claims that share a `service_identity`.

controllers.description:
Every control pathway to this entity — the provider(s) that can observe
and act on it. A single-provider node carries one entry; when the same
logical container is reported by more than one provider on the same host
(docker's socket AND unraid's GraphQL; docker AND dockge) all pathways
are preserved so callers can tell whether it is controllable over
docker, dockge, both, or unraid. Never collapsed to one — mirrors
`unit::UnitSource`.

endpoints.description: Endpoints (ports) this workload listens on. Passthrough from the claim.

id.description: Synthetic stable id: `claim:{provider}:{provider_instance}:{kind}:{native_id}`.

image.description: Container image / template ref, when known. Passthrough from the claim.

label.description: Display name — guest hostname, container name, or stack name.

labels.description: Provider labels/metadata. Passthrough from the claim.

nativeId.description: Provider-native id (proxmox vmid, docker short id, stack name).

allOf.description:
Network addresses this entity is reachable at. Passthrough from the
claim; same channel vocabulary peers carry.

runsOn.description: Hostname of the node this entity runs on, when the provider reports it.

service.description:
The runtime service identity correlated to this node by `(host, port)`,
when a registration matches one of its endpoints.

serviceIdentity.description:
Host-scoped compose-stack correlation key (a DESCRIPTIVE attribute, not
an id). Passthrough from `TopologyClaim.service_identity`; the key used
to group this container under a synthesized `stack` node. `None` on a
stack node itself and on claims the provider can't attribute to a stack.

serviceRole.description:
Service role after correlation: a matched runtime registration wins over
the provider's claim hint.

state.description:
Normalized runtime run-state (`"running"`/`"stopped"`/`"paused"`) when
the provider reports it. Passthrough from the claim; drives the
topology node's `status`.

endpoint.description:
Logical endpoint name (e.g. the proxmox endpoint the cluster was
fetched from). Multiple endpoints can report the same cluster.

name.description: Cluster name. `None` for standalone hosts that report no cluster.

ClusterSummary.description:
Cluster header summary. Online/total counts derived from
`contract::ClusterRoster::list_clusters()`.

nested.description: True when one path nests under the other (vs an exact same-folder clash).

Container.description:
Normalized container row — the unit every adapter returns and every
reconciler consumes.

Field selection is the §2.1 minimum needed to decide an action:

- `id` / `name` / `runtime` / `host` — identity and dispatch.
- `state` / `restart_policy` — auto-start decision.
- `image` — surfaced for operator context and crashloop classification.
- `labels` — `orca.skip`, `orca.heal=manual`, `orca.heal.drain=long`
  gates live here (§2.1 + §2.2 active-write drain).
- `mounts` — dep-graph input for the mounts reconciler.
- `ports` — surfaced for inventory aggregation; not used by the §2.1
  loop directly.
- `started_at` / `finished_at` — crashloop window math (§2.1 circuit
  breaker).
- `restart_count` — same.
- `exit_code` — distinguishes clean exit from crash for the breaker.
- `startup` — boot ordering (LXC), feeds the §2.2 forward/reverse
  restart sequence.

finishedAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp the container last exited.

allOf.description:
Operational health, populated by runtime adapters per the layered
precedence rule in [`contract::health`]. Defaults to
[`contract::health::Health::Unknown`] until an adapter reports.

host.description:
Hostname of the machine running this container. Stamped by the
adapter from the local host's identity at list time; downstream
consumers (sort, inventory aggregator) key on this without an
additional hop. Empty string is reserved for the "unknown host"
case where the adapter couldn't determine its own hostname.

startedAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp the container last entered `Running`.

startup.description:
Boot-time ordering hints (LXC only today). `None` when the runtime
has no ordering primitive (docker).

ContainerCreateAction.description:
The `container.create` action. `exec` is the only one — it keeps the
six-verb `create{action=…}` shape and the exec-specific deny-by-default
gating unchanged (this tool is admin-gated and mesh-exec dispatchable exactly
as `containers.exec` was; renaming the verb does not weaken either axis).

oneOf.description: Run a one-shot command inside a container/CT.

ContainerDetailView.description:
Which facet `container.detail` reports. `logs` (tail) is the first; more
views fold in here as the enum grows.

ContainerMount.description:
One bind mount or volume on a container. The mount source is the key the
mounts reconciler uses to build the (mount → dependents) edge for the
dep graph ([[self-healing-reconciler.md]] §2.2).

readOnly.description: True when the mount is read-only.

protocol.description:
`"tcp"` / `"udp"`. Free-form to admit runtime-specific values without
constraining the model prematurely.

ContainerState.description:
Observed lifecycle state, normalized across runtimes.

docker's full set (`created`, `restarting`, `running`, `removing`, `paused`,
`exited`, `dead`) maps directly. lxc's `STOPPED`/`RUNNING`/`FROZEN`/`ABORTING`/
`STARTING`/`STOPPING` map to the closest equivalents.

oneOf.description:
Created but never started (docker `created`, lxc `STOPPED` for a
freshly-created CT).
Mid-start.
Live and (per runtime) considered running.
Paused / frozen.
Currently shutting down.

Stopped after running. Distinguished from `Created` because the
reconciler treats clean exits and crashloops differently (§2.1
auto-start vs circuit breaker).

Runtime reports the container as dead / unrecoverable without
re-creation.

Runtime returned a state string we have no mapping for. Recorded
verbatim so operators can see what the raw value was — the reconciler
treats this as "do not act" rather than guessing.

ContainerUpdateAction.description:
The `container.update` action. Folds the former imperative container verbs
(`containers.reconcile` / `reconcile_dry` / `unhold` / `unwedge`) onto the
six-verb `update{action=…}` shape.

oneOf.description: One reconcile pass across every registered adapter.
Plan-only reconcile: classify + probe (read-only), never start.
Clear a `Held` breaker record so the reconciler stops short-circuiting.
Manually trigger recovery for a wedged container.

ContainersUnholdOutput.description:
Tool-facing view of a cleared `BreakerRecord`. Flattened to the
fields an operator cares about; timestamps are RFC 3339 strings
(`Container` uses the same string-projection pattern at
`lib.rs:220-240`).

previouslyHeldSince.description:
`held_since` from the cleared record, RFC 3339. `None` if the
record's prior held_since was unset (shouldn't happen for a
real Held record, but the type doesn't enforce that).

ContainersUnwedgeOutput.description:
Outcome of one `unwedge` action. Flat — `Liveness` is projected to strings
at the boundary just like the runtime field.

attemptDurationSecs.description: Wall-clock seconds from start of the attempt to post-probe.

error.description:
Adapter error message when the recovery call itself failed.
`None` when the recovery call returned Ok, regardless of
`recovered`.

postProbe.description:
`live` / `wedged` / `unknown` / `not_applicable` — what
liveness reported after the recovery call returned.

recovered.description: True iff the post-attempt liveness probe came back `Live`.

Controller.description:
A single control pathway to a synthesized entity: the provider (and which
instance of it) through which the entity can be observed and acted on.

nativeId.description:
Provider-native id under this pathway; may differ across providers for
the same logical entity.

DaemonRuntimeStatus.description:
Runtime snapshot of the orca daemon (pid/port/uptime + liveness).

Surfaced as `system.detail.daemon`. The `version`, `mode`, and binary
path fields callers might expect already live on the parent
`SystemStatusReport` (sourced from the daemon state file) — don't
duplicate them here.

DbDetailView.description:
Which facet `db.detail` reports. `summary` (schema version + pending count)
is the default; `stats` returns per-table storage cost.

applied.description: Number of migrations applied (or rolled back) in this call.

totalBytes.description: Total bytes across all user tables (sum of `tables[].bytes`).

current.description:
Highest applied migration version (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS timestamp, or 0 if
only the apply_schema baseline has run).

total.description: Total migrations compiled into this orca binary.

oneOf.description: Apply all pending migrations.
Apply the next pending migration (one step).
Revert the most recently applied migration (one step).
Retention sweep: delete rows older than `days` from `table`.
Reclaim disk space (full `VACUUM`, or `incremental`).

id.description: Runtime-native id the target assigned (CT id, container id, VMID).

DiskHealth.description:
Disk headroom for the filesystem hosting `~/.orca`, so a near-full host or
CI runner is visible over `--peer` before it wedges.

path.description: Mount point of the filesystem hosting `~/.orca`.

usedPct.description: Percent used, round((total-avail)/total*100); 0 when total is 0.

Drain.description:
Drain policy — how a source is released from every client before a
coordinated operation (a source reboot) that will take it offline.

enabled.description: Whether a coordinated drain is performed at all.

allOf.description: Lazy vs lazy-force unmount.

settleSecs.description:
Seconds to wait after the lazy unmount before the forced one, letting
in-flight I/O settle.

DrainMode.description: How a coordinated drain releases every client placement of a source.

oneOf.description: `umount -l` (lazy): detach the mount, letting in-flight I/O finish.
`umount -l -f` (lazy + force): detach even under a wedged/held handle.

host.description: Deploy-target host the instance runs on.

instance.description: Instance name, unique within the provider.

method.description:
Backup method override (`tar`/`pbs`/…). Absent = auto-select (a Proxmox
LXC/VM with PBS available routes to `pbs`, else `tar`).

routes.description:
Reachability routes, repeatable, each `kind:scheme://host[:port]` — e.g.
`lan_v4:http://10.0.0.5:8990`, `fqdn:https://sonarr.example.com`,
`tailscale_v4:http://100.64.0.5:8990`, `wireguard_v4:http://10.0.0.5:8990`.
`kind` is any label (nothing whitelists kinds); the `lan_v4` route's port
is the host bind for `workload_spec`, the rest are reach paths. Order is
priority (index 0 = primary).

runtime.description:
Runtime the instance runs as (`docker`/`podman`/`lxc`/`vm`). Drives the
backup path; absent = the backend's first declared runtime.

ExportRow.description:
An export a host serves, tagged with the backend that publishes it. Flat
projection of [`plugin_toolkit::storage::ExportEntry`].

ExternalId.description:
One external identifier that canonicalizes the work. The MERGE KEY: two
variants sharing any `(source, id)` are the same unit.

Failover.description: Fail-over / fail-back policy between a mount's ordered sources.

confirmTicks.description:
Consecutive confirming ticks a transition must persist before it is acted
on — the blip filter that rides out a briefly-slow server.

enabled.description:
Whether ordered-source fail-over is performed at all. When `false` the
mount stays pinned to its primary source and is never re-elected.

allOf.description: Which transport-liveness probe the election uses.

returnToPrimary.description:
Whether to fail *back* to a higher-priority source once it is live again
(index 0 = primary wins the next election). When `false`, a mount that
degraded to a secondary stays there until it too fails.

error.description: Per-plugin error. The fan-out continues past it.

host.description: Display hostname of the host.

installed.description: Installed version on the host, or `None` when not installed.

name.description: Plugin / target-software name.

note.description: Human-readable note — e.g. why an unreleased/sideloaded plugin was skipped.

target.description: Newest version resolved for the plugin.

updateAvailable.description: True when `target` is strictly newer than `installed`.

updated.description: True when this plugin was actually (re)installed (execute only).

applied.description: Version applied (execute only); `None` on a dry run or no-op.

blocked.description:
True when the host structurally cannot fetch a release asset — no local
`github_token` and no trusted peer to delegate through (#652). A row can
be both `update_available` and `blocked`: a newer version exists, and
THIS host cannot obtain it. Read them together before `--execute`.

blockedReason.description: Why [`Self::blocked`] is set, naming the remedies. `None` when not blocked.

current.description: Current daemon version probed on the host.

error.description: Per-host error (probe/apply/health-gate). The fan-out continues past it.

host.description: Display hostname of the host.

id.description:
The system's id; empty for the local host.

Systems are addressed by this id, and orca resolves routes to reach them.
It is the same value `system.health` reports as `machineId`, and it is
stored in `mesh_peers.peer_id` pending that table's rename to `systems`.

target.description: Channel-latest the host would move to.

updateAvailable.description: True when `target` is strictly newer than `current`.

errors.description: Fan-out-level errors (peer enumeration, etc.), distinct from per-host ones.

runRecord.description:
Absolute path of the run record this fan-out writes after every host.
Surfaced as a field, not only as a note, because it is the ONLY way a
caller recovers the outcome of an `execute` roll: the last act of the
roll restarts the local daemon and severs the caller's connection
(#625). `None` when no orca home was resolvable.

systems.description: Per-host daemon update plan/results, in apply order (local last).

GpuInfo.description: One GPU detected on the host.

driverInstallHint.description:
Suggested package to install to get full metrics. Distro-specific;
only populated when `driver_status = "no_driver"` or `"no_metrics"`.

driverStatus.description:
Driver/tool availability: `"ok"` when metrics are live, `"no_driver"`
when the GPU was detected via sysfs/PCI but the user-space driver or
query tool is absent, `"no_metrics"` when the driver is loaded but
doesn't expose utilization (e.g. Intel iGPU without `intel_gpu_top`).

name.description: Display name from driver (e.g. `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090`).

GpuPoint.description:
One GPU's reading inside a `SystemHistoryPoint`. Matched to a live
`GpuInfo` by `name` (driver-stable across ticks).

GraphqlProxyResult.description: `body` is opaque — GraphQL response shapes vary per query and are not owned by orca.

Health.description:
Operational health of a thing (container, service, host, …). Populated per
the layered precedence rule documented on this module.

oneOf.description: Working as intended — the native check or declared probe passes.
Coming up — inside its start-period / warm-up window, not yet Healthy.
Working but impaired — some checks fail while it still serves.
Not working — the native check or declared probe fails.
The signal applies but has not yet been determined (no report yet).
No health signal applies — neither a native check nor a declared probe.

HealthReport.description:
Lean host liveness/health probe returned by `system.health`. Cheap enough to
answer at memory speed on any host, and peer-dispatchable so a controller can
probe a remote host's health over the mesh (`orca --peer <host> system
health`). This is the reframed replacement for the retired user-facing
`mesh ping` ("ping applies to a host, not the mesh"); the same daemon
liveness + identity/version signals the wire probe reported, surfaced as a
first-class typed host-health verb.

checkedAtMs.description: Unix epoch milliseconds this probe was taken.

allOf.description: Runtime snapshot: running / pid / port / uptime_seconds.

disk.description:
Headroom of the filesystem hosting `~/.orca`. `None` when the probe
fails or no mount matches — a disk probe error never fails the health
call, and older decoders ignore the field.

displayName.description:
Operator-visible host name (display_name channel, falling back to OS
hostname).

healthy.description: True when the orca daemon is running on this host.

version.description: orca version from `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` at build time.

name.description: `None` = ungrouped bucket (rendered last).

Location.description:
Where bytes physically live — a reference into the storage domain. The same
variant may exist in several locations (replicated across shares/hosts).

host.description: Host the path is realized on, when known.

path.description: Absolute path to the file on that storage.

storageBackend.description: Storage-domain provider name backing this path (`nfs` / `smb`), when known.

level.description:
Best-effort parsed severity (`error`|`warn`|`info`|`debug`|`trace`),
or `None` for lines with no recognizable level token.

message.description: The full raw line, trailing newline trimmed.

MediaCapability.description:
Capability strings a backend advertises (domain-interpreted). Carries both the
role markers and the concrete verbs; the media crate parses them off
`BackendDef::capabilities`. Role markers (`DownloadedBy`/`ServedBy`) double as
capabilities so a backend's role set is derivable from `capabilities()` alone,
mirroring how the `web` domain rides existing `BackendDef` axes with no new
ABI field.

oneOf.description: Return reachable base URL(s) for device setup.
Return per-user credentials (orca-managed) for device setup.
Enumerate the backend's library for this media type.
Free-text search (acquisition or library lookup).
Add an item to the library (queue a download / import a file).
Remove an item from the library.
Re-match / fix an item's metadata identity.
Report acquisition/library status.

Contribute this backend's partial [`MediaUnit`] view (identity +
variants + how it serves them) for cross-backend convergence.

Re-read ONE item from disk after an acquirer mutated its path. Scoped to
the affected item deliberately: a whole-library refresh is minutes of IO
per PROPER upgrade, and upgrades are routine.

MediaCredentials.description:
Per-user credentials for a served-by backend, so a device can be set up. The
password is a [`SecretRef`] the secrets domain resolves — the media backend
never inlines a plaintext secret. orca owns/propagates the actual value.

passwordRef.description:
Reference to the password secret (resolved via the secrets domain), if the
backend uses a password. Never a plaintext value on the wire.

allOf.description: Reachable URL(s) to point the device at.

username.description: The username orca manages for this user on this backend.

MediaIdentity.description: What a unit IS — the identity every variant resolves to.

externalIds.description: Canonical external ids — the cross-server/​cross-format merge keys.

series.description: Series/sequence position, when part of a series.

MediaProvider.description: A descriptor row for one registered media backend — the `media.*` list view.

allOf.description: The media type this registration handles.

name.description: App identity (`audiobookshelf`, `lazylibrarian`, `plex`).

roles.description: Roles this backend plays for the type.

MediaRole.description:
The role a backend plays *for a given media type* — the second axis of the
domain. A backend may play both (rare, e.g. plex serves and can request).

oneOf.description: Acquirer: searches for and downloads/queues this media type.
Server/player-backend: serves/streams this media type to devices.

MediaType.description:
The media *type* axis — carried on `BackendDef::kind`. This is the primary
axis the aggregation surface groups by (`media.detail --media-type audiobooks`).

MediaUnit.description:
THE convergence object: a canonical piece of media with everything known about
it — what it is, its variants (resolutions/formats/tracks), where the
bytes live, and who serves it and how. Assembled by merging each backend's
partial view (see [`merge_units`]) by [`MediaIdentity`] external ids.

downloadedBy.description:
Acquirer app name(s) that actually contributed a view of THIS unit — the
per-unit half of the relation, which the media-type registration cannot
answer ("sonarr can acquire tv" ≠ "sonarr got this episode").

servedBy.description:
Server app name(s) that actually hold/serve THIS unit. Narrower than
`sources`, which also carries method+url and raw file-share sourcing.

MediaUrl.description:
A reachable URL for a served-by backend, for device setup. `primary` is the
best guess; `alternates` are additional reachable paths (LAN, tailscale, FQDN).

oneOf.description: Dial the inviter directly and auto-accept (needs `addr`).
Push an offer to an mDNS-discovered joiner (needs `addr`).
Complete an out-of-band offer by its printed code (needs `code`).
Evict a paired peer (needs `peer_id`).
Voluntary self exit. LOCAL-ONLY.
Hard-delete a stale/orphan peer mesh-wide (needs `peer_id`).

discoveryState.description:
mDNS-advertised membership: `"unclaimed"` or `"mesh:<mesh_id>"`. Named
`discovery_state` (not `state`) so it doesn't collide with the
`#[serde(tag = "state")]` discriminant on [`MeshMember`], which would
otherwise clobber the `"discovered"` tag and break state filtering.

peerId.description: A live member we asked to forget the target.

rowsRemoved.description: Rows deleted on THIS host across mesh_peers/mesh_trust/mesh_discovery/offers.

MeshHealthReport.description:
Health of every system in the mesh — what a bare `orca system health`
answers.

MeshHealthRow.description: One system's row in a mesh-wide health report.

error.description:
Why this system could not be reported on. The sweep continues past it,
so one unreachable system never hides the health of the rest.

health.description: The system's own health report. `None` when it could not be reached.

host.description: Display hostname of the system.

id.description: The system's id; empty for the local system, which has no roster row.

MeshInstance.description:
Fully-shaped instance row the frontend systems UI renders directly, in the
same camelCase wire form as the rest of the surface so the typed SDK from
regen flows through unchanged.

availableVersions.description:
Full version list from a `system.update {}` probe. Always empty on
this endpoint — the page-level probe overlay populates it client-side.

lastChecked.description: Wall-clock millis when this row was assembled.

origin.description:
For the synthetic local row this is emitted as `""` — the frontend
overwrites it with `window.location.origin` after fetch since the
daemon doesn't know how the browser reached it. Remote rows carry the
`addr:port` of the peer.

reachableAddrs.description:
LAN addresses reachable by the browser. Computed server-side from
`addresses` + `system` to replace the JS `reachableAddrs()` helper.

role.description: `"local"` for the synthetic self row, `"system"` for every paired peer.

rowsRemoved.description: Number of peer rows removed from `mesh_peers` (one per paired peer).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or absent on the last page.

MeshMember.description:
Unified mesh-membership view. Every row carries a `state` discriminant so
callers see joined members, in-flight handshakes, and mDNS-discovered
candidates in one shape. Replaces the previous trio of `system.peer.list`,
`system.peer.discovery.list`, and `system.peer.handshake.list` (2026-05-28
consolidation).

allOf.description:
Paired mesh member — full mTLS peer with addressing, runtime info, and
(when probed) ping latency + topology facts. Boxed because the joined
row carries more fields than the other variants; without the
indirection the whole enum pays that size on every row.
Pending inbound or outbound offer — pairing handshake in progress.
mDNS-discovered orca that is not yet paired.

code.description:
Pairing code minted for this offer; show to the operator so they can
run `system.join --action accept` on the joiner side.

addr.description:
Legacy single dial address. No longer serialized — every address now
lives in `addresses` as an equal channel (there is no privileged
"primary" address). Kept as a `serde(default)` inbound field so rosters
from pre-collapse peers (which still send `addr`) still deserialize, and
as an internal fallback until every peer advertises a full `addresses`
snapshot. The shaping layer folds this value into `addresses` so nothing
is lost when it stops being serialized.

latencyMs.description: Round-trip latency of the `mesh/ping` probe, milliseconds.

local.description:
True for the synthetic local-host row prepended to `system.list`. Remote
peers are always false. Lets UIs flag "this is me" without string
matching the hostname.

probeError.description:
Error string from the probe path (ping / runtime-spec / update-check).
First failure wins so the UI has one line to surface.

pubkeyFp.description:
Bootstrap-pubkey fingerprint of this peer, as known to the responder.
Propagated through roster sync so peers learned via intermediary can
transitively pin the fp instead of arriving with `None` — without
this, mesh/exec from a roster-synced peer is refused with "no pinned
bootstrap key" forever after.

reachable.description:
`mesh/ping` succeeded inside the fanout budget. `None` when probing was
skipped (e.g. departed peers); `Some(false)` when the dial errored.

allOf.description:
Multi-channel routes (LAN v4/v6, Tailscale, FQDN, …) as shared
[`Route`]s. May be empty for peers paired before slice 4 of the
host-addressing plan landed.

system.description:
Lean topology facts (hostname/type/cluster/virt/macs/claims/primary IPs)
projected from the peer's `system.detail`. Drives parent-inference,
cluster grouping, and host-card rendering without the fat host snapshot
(which lives on `system.info.detail`). `None` when the probe failed.

updateAvailable.description:
True when an update is available for the peer (and not blocked by
`pinned_to`).

updateCheckedSecs.description:
Age in seconds of the last successful `system.update {}` probe against
this peer. `None` until the periodic probe has succeeded at least
once (or for the synthetic local-host row).

updateLatest.description:
Latest release tag visible to the peer on its channel. Pulled from
`system.update-check`; `None` when the probe failed or timed out.

cleared.description:
`true` if a `departed_at` flag was actually cleared. `false` means the
peer either wasn't departed or doesn't exist locally.

candidates.description: mDNS-discovered, unclaimed, not a self-echo, not already paired.

clusterMembership.description:
`peer_id` → cluster name for every joined peer matched to a cluster
via IP-first then hostname. Only matches included.

clusters.description: Plugin-neutral cluster roster (proxmox today; others later).

inboundOffers.description: Handshaking offers whose `expires_at` is still in the future.

members.description: Same shape as `system.list.members` — the UI reuses the existing type.

stale.description: Departed joined peers + discovered orphans + stale self-identities.

mutual.description:
True when both sides trust each other. Secure peers can sync
credentials; non-mutual peers only retain their own credentials.

oneOf.description: Toggle `self_secure` (Tier-2 secrets-storage). Default.
Set trust for a paired peer (needs `peer_id` + `on`).
Force a one-shot replication tick (optional `peer` filter).

Clear a stale `departed_at` flag on THIS host (needs `peer_id`).
LOCAL-ONLY.
Clear stuck outbound pairing offer(s) for `addr`.

apiKeyInDb.description:
True when an API key is stored for this model. The key value is
never returned; callers see only presence.

MountHealth.description:
Liveness classification for a mountpoint. Shared so the nfs/smb dashboards
speak one language.

oneOf.description: Path is a live mount and answers I/O within the budget.
Mount is present but I/O hung past the timeout (unreachable server).
Path does not exist / nothing mounted there.
Probe exceeded its time budget without a definite stale/ok answer.
Probe failed for some other reason.

Mount is live and readable, but a write was denied (EACCES/EPERM/EROFS).
The share drifted to a mode/owner that leaves the mounting identity
without write access — reads succeed, so plain [`probe_health`] reports
`Ok`, yet consumers that write (uploads, renames, lock files) fail. Only
[`probe_writable`] surfaces this. A remount does NOT fix it (the drift is
server-side); the remediation is a server-side chmod/chown, so callers
must treat this as *present* — never as stale/missing that triggers a
remount or failover.

State is not observed by the daemon answering the read: the placement
belongs to another host and that owner could not be reached to report its
own liveness. Distinct from `Missing` (a definite "nothing is mounted"),
which only the owning host can assert. A read never presents a peer's
host-local liveness column as truth — an unreached owner is `Unknown`.

MountOutcome.description:
Result of a mount/unmount operation. `recovered` is set when the backend had
to run its stale-handle recovery sequence (lazy unmount + remount) to reach
the requested state — surfaced so the reconciler can record self-healing.

MountRef.description:
A reference to another table's row — a field that points at `<table>.id`
carries the id nested under the table's name, never a bare `shareId`/`hostId`
([[no-top-level-urls-use-addresses-array]] sibling: reference-object rule).

MountRoute.description:
One of a share's canonical routes, projected onto a placement with its live
state. The addressing fields (`kind`/`value`/`port`/`path`/`enabled`) come
from `shares.routes`; `active`/`options`/`drift` are this host's tick-observed
reality for the route currently mounted at the target.

active.description:
Whether THIS route is the source currently mounted at the target — the
route self-annotating, replacing the old top-level `activeRoute` scalar.

drift.description:
Whether the active route's live options diverge from the share's rendered
options ("has this host drifted, still `hard`?"). Always `false` on a
non-active route.

options.description:
Comma-joined live `-o` option tokens the kernel reports, present only on
the active route (the STORED value the tick observed, so an operator sees
hard-vs-soft per host without SSHing in).

MountView.description:
A `mounts` placement projected for the API: the true PK `id`, the per-host
`name` label, and `share` / `host` as nested id references.

allOf.description:
Last-known liveness, written by the convergence tick — the STORED value,
never a live probe (the read path takes no fan-out).

multiMounted.description:
Whether the convergence tick observed more than one mount stacked at this
target (an anomaly: the write path blocks it, a reconcile tolerates and
surfaces it here). More than one `active` route implies the same.

routes.description:
The share's canonical routes (failover candidates), each annotated with
this placement's live state. **The route self-annotates `active`** — there
is no separate `activeRoute` scalar. Derived read-only from the joined
share; a placement owns no routes of its own. Empty if the share is gone.

NodeSource.description:
A node's identity. Either an orca **peer** (runs the daemon, has a full
`system` snapshot) or a **claim** — a non-peer entity (guest VM/LXC,
container, compose stack) that a host reports running but which does not
itself run orca. Claim nodes are synthesized from `system.claims[]`.

oneOf.description: Raise (create or reactivate) a stateful dismissable notification.
Poll every registered external source and reconcile into the store.
Fire an ephemeral event through the installed dispatcher (no state).

notification.description: The updated notification, or `null` if no notification had that key.

sourceDismiss.description:
Present when the dismissed notification was pushed back to its external
source (the source is registered, supports dismiss-at-source, and the
row carries a `source_ref`). Absent for local-only dismisses.

configured.description:
True when the global dispatcher was installed and ran. False when
notifications are unconfigured on this host (no backends to send to).

oneOf.description: Dismiss a notification (user acknowledged it).
Suppress a notification permanently ("ignore permanently").
Run the diagnostics→notification reconcile pass.

OwnerCandidate.description:
A candidate OWNER inferred from reference peers — "N comparable shares are
owned by this uid:gid". Presented the same way as [`PermCandidate`] and, like
it, never applied automatically.

Ownership needs its own candidate type because it drifts INDEPENDENTLY of
mode, and drifting alone is enough to break writes: on 2026-09-25 a PBS
datastore had correct modes throughout and one directory owned by 99:100
instead of 34:34, so every prune unlink failed with `Permission denied` while
mode-only detection reported nothing wrong (#620).

count.description: How many reference peers use it (the evidence weight).

gid.description: Owning gid the reference peers carry.

samplePaths.description: A few example peer paths, so the choice is auditable.

uid.description: Owning uid the reference peers carry.

oneOf.description: Debian/Ubuntu — requires dpkg-deb
RHEL/Fedora/Unraid — requires rpmbuild
Alpine — writes APKBUILD, requires abuild
Arch/AUR — writes PKGBUILD, no build tool required
macOS Installer — requires pkgbuild (Xcode CLT), optional productsign
Homebrew — writes a formula .rb file, no build tool required

Unraid — writes a `.plg` plugin manifest. Lifecycle is driven by
emhttpd event hooks (disks_mounted -> start, stopping_svcs -> stop)
so Unraid owns clean startup AND shutdown, retiring the
/boot/config/go SHFS-poll hook. See
[[project-unraid-plugin-install-blocked-on-graphql]] and
[[project-orca-unraid-unclean-shutdown]].

PathChange.description:
How an acquirer mutated the file — enough for a server to decide whether to
re-read, re-locate, or forget the item.

oneOf.description: Upgraded in place under a new name (the PROPER/REPACK case).
Same bytes, new name (a rename/organize pass).
Gone with no successor — the library row is now orphaned.
New file with no predecessor (a fresh import).

PeerSyncReport.description:
Per-peer outcome of a single sync (push or pull). `orca system mesh update --action sync` returns these
directly so operators see exactly what happened.

PermCandidate.description:
A candidate mode inferred from reference peers — "N comparable shares use this
mode, here are examples". The repair presents these, ranked by evidence, for a
human to confirm; it is never applied automatically.

count.description: How many reference peers use it (the evidence weight).

mode.description: The mode the reference peers carry.

samplePaths.description: A few example peer paths that use it, so the choice is auditable.

mode.description: Permission bits (the low 12: rwx triples + setuid/setgid/sticky).

Placement.description:
A set of opaque placement labels describing where a workload runs, consulted
by a target's `fits()` to decide whether to offer that target
([[topology-must-model-guest-services]]). It informs which targets are
offered; it never gates a user's explicit choice.

A plugin that manages a platform assigns the label it owns (e.g. the Proxmox
plugin tags a host `"proxmox"`), and that plugin's target `fits()` is the code
that interprets it. Labels are meaningful only to the `fits()` that checks for
them ([[orca-core-generic-plugins-expose-functionality]]).

host.description: The host the workload runs on, if known.

labels.description:
Opaque placement labels, plugin-assigned (e.g. `"proxmox"`). Core does not
interpret them; a target's `fits()` checks for the labels it understands.

oneOf.description: Install a plugin (sideload `--file` or catalog `--name`).
Invoke a loaded plugin verb by name (the generic mesh seam).

synced.description: `true` once the credential has been synced to the plugin runtime.

oneOf.description: Remove a plugin: delete its executable and unregister its tools.

installedPath.description: Absolute path the plugin executable was copied to in the install dir.

loadedLive.description: True — sideload registers tools immediately, no restart needed.

tools.description: Tools registered live by the install.

result.description: The plugin verb's return value, verbatim.

PluginListRow.description:
One thin row in `plugin.list`: identity + status + a tool COUNT (never the
full tool array — that lives on `plugin.detail`, keeping list thin + fast).

catalog.description: Catalog metadata, when this name is a known first-party plugin.

name.description: Plugin / target-software name.

sideloaded.description: True when this plugin is not in the catalog (a sideloaded third party).

allOf.description:
Whether the plugin is a known first-party catalog entry, sideloaded, or
merely planned.

toolCount.description:
Number of tools this plugin contributes when loaded (0 otherwise). The
tool NAMES are on `plugin.detail`.

oneOf.description: Present on disk and currently loaded in-process.
In the catalog but neither installed nor loaded.

Installed on disk but not loaded — usually a failed compat gate, or
installed after startup with no live registration yet.

dataKeys.description: Stored data keys (values fetched via `plugin.data.detail` with `data_key`).

detail.description: What is wrong, in one sentence.

source.description: Where it was found, when tied to a specific rule.

PrivilegeRule.description: One parsed privilege rule, from either sudoers or doas.

isGroup.description: True when `principal` names a group rather than a user.

nopasswd.description: Whether the rule skips password entry (`NOPASSWD:` / doas `nopass`).

principal.description: Who the rule grants to: a username, or `%group` / `:group` for a group.

system.description:
Which system advertises this provider. Empty = this one.

The surface is the FLEET's, not this host's: a provider is only
actionable if you know where it lives, and the operator must never
have to name a host to find out.

systemErrors.description:
Systems that could not be asked. Non-empty means this listing is
INCOMPLETE — "no such provider" means something different when part of
the fleet was never reached.

ReconcileAction.description:
Closed enum of actions the reconciler can take per container. The
reconciler stamps exactly one of these per candidate row; opaque
blob variants are deliberately absent ([[feedback-no-serde-json-value]]).

oneOf.description:
Container was successfully started (or, in dry mode, would have
been started).
Restart policy is `no`/`on-failure`; reconciler left it alone.

Container carries `orca.skip=true` or `orca.heal=manual`;
reconciler left it alone.

At least one bind mount source returned ESTALE; the start was
gated and the container left in its observed state.

Container was a tentative start (exited non-zero) and the
breaker returned [`BreakerDecision::Hold`]. C3 wires this but
the stub breaker never returns it; C4 flips it on.

Candidate not eligible — already running, paused, mid-
transition, or in an unknown state.

ReconcileOutput.description:
Result of one reconcile pass — typed, exhaustively enumerated, no
opaque JSON value types anywhere on the surface.

adapterErrors.description:
Adapter `list()` failures. An adapter erroring on `list` does
not fail the whole reconcile.

dryRun.description:
True when the call ran in dry mode (no `.start()` calls, no
breaker arming). Stale-mount probes still ran — they're read-
only.

rows.description: One row per container the reconciler considered.

startErrors.description:
Adapter `start()` failures captured during execution. Empty in
dry mode.

ReconcileReason.description:
Typed reason field on a [`ReconcileRow`]. Each variant carries
exactly the context the operator needs to understand the action.

oneOf.description: Started, no breaker involvement.

Started after a non-zero exit; breaker armed and returned
`Proceed`.
Restart policy is `no`/`on-failure`.
`orca.skip=true` or `orca.heal=manual` label override.
Stale mount(s) blocked the start.
Breaker returned `Hold` for a tentative start.
Container is in a state the reconciler does not act on.

ReconcileRow.description:
One row in [`ReconcileOutput::rows`]: the action the reconciler
took (or would have taken in dry mode) for one container.

RemediationPolicy.description:
Whether orca's self-healing controllers may act automatically on this host.

Variants order from most to least autonomous. `Default` is `Notify` (via
`#[default]`, so the derived impl satisfies the workspace `derivable_impls`
lint rather than a hand-written `impl Default`).

oneOf.description: Controller remediates automatically, silently.
Controller remediates automatically AND emits a notification of what was done.

Controller does NOT act; emits a dismissable notification carrying the
PROPOSED remediation action for user approval.
Controller does not act and does not notify (silent).

RemountAggression.description:
How aggressively a re-election is allowed to disrupt an *actively-held* mount
when failing (back) to the elected source.

Remounting under live container I/O can interrupt Plex/Jellyfin mid-stream,
so the aggressiveness is a policy, and the default is [`Safe`](Self::Safe).

oneOf.description:
Never disturb a busy mount. If the elected source differs from the live
one and the mount is busy, re-render and log a *pending* failback; the
swap happens on the next idle re-trigger. A not-busy mount is remounted
immediately. This is the default.

Prefer a clean remount, but if the mount is busy escalate to a lazy
force-unmount + retrigger (and, only as a clearly-logged last resort,
killing holders). Opt-in per mount — it can disrupt live I/O.

RemountPolicy.description:
The typed per-mount remount policy — the whole engine's behaviour axis in one
serde object, replacing the opaque `remount_policy` string.

allOf.description: How aggressively a re-election may disrupt a busy mount.
Coordinated-drain policy.
Ordered-source fail-over / fail-back policy.

ReplicationStatus.description:
Observed sync health of one replication relationship, measured host-local and
on-demand (never a poll-cache). The failover-safety gate consults `healthy`;
`last_sync_ms` / `detail` are for surfacing ("willow↔maple 100%, synced 2m
ago").

detail.description:
Human-readable state for display / diagnostics, when the provider offers
one. Never secrets.

healthy.description:
Whether every member of the relationship is currently in sync — the one
signal the failover gate requires before permitting an active-route swap.

lastSyncMs.description:
Epoch-millis of the last confirmed sync across members, when the provider
tracks it ([[time-values-in-milliseconds]]).

RescanOutcome.description:
Per-backend result of one path-invalidation fan-out. A backend that refused or
was unreachable is a row here, not a failed call.

error.description: Non-fatal failure from this one backend.

ok.description: Whether that backend accepted and performed the rescan.

provider.description: Backend app name that was asked.

RescanTarget.description:
Which item to rescan, carrying BOTH locators because backends disagree on how
they address an item: Plex/Jellyfin can refresh a path subtree, while
identity-keyed servers (ABS, komga) only know external ids. Either locator
alone is enough to act on — see [`RescanTarget::is_addressable`] — so an
acquirer supplies whatever it has rather than the intersection.

allOf.description: What changed. `Deleted` means "drop/re-locate", not "re-read".

external_ids.description: Identity locator: canonical external ids of the affected work.

old_path.description:
Path locator, pre-mutation. Present for `Replaced`/`Renamed`/`Deleted` —
this is the string a stale library row still holds, so it is what a
path-keyed backend matches on.

title.description:
Human-readable title, for logs and for backends that can only fuzzy-match.
Never a locator on its own.

RestartPolicy.description:
Restart policy as declared by the runtime, normalized across docker / lxc /
podman / nspawn.

The reconciler treats `UnlessStopped` and `Always` as "desired = running"
(§2.1 source of truth). `No` and `OnFailure` are read-only signals — the
reconciler will not auto-restart these.

oneOf.description: `--restart no` (docker), `lxc.start.auto=0` (lxc), etc.
`--restart on-failure[:max-retries]`.
`--restart unless-stopped`.
`--restart always`, `lxc.start.auto=1`.

rows.description:
A single row with `peerId=None` representing the (single-host) global
retention policy. The list shape is kept for wire compatibility; there
are no per-peer rows anymore — host_status is local-only.

days.description: Resolved age cap in days. Always present (falls back to built-in default).

maxMb.description: Resolved size cap in megabytes. `None` = unlimited.

maxRows.description: Resolved row count cap. Always present (falls back to safety guard).

peerId.description: `None` for the global default row, `Some(peer)` for a per-peer override.

schedulerRunsPerJob.description:
Instance-global: rows kept per job in `scheduler_runs`. Populated only
on the global (peerId=null) view; `None` for per-peer rows.

sessionEventsDays.description:
Instance-global: `session_events` retention window in days. Populated
only on the global (peerId=null) view; `None` for per-peer rows.

Route.description:
One reachable path to an addressable thing.

The URL is reconstructed at resolve time as `scheme://value[:port]` — the
pieces are stored separately so there is no scalar URL to drift, and so a
per-plugin scheme (a websocket `ws://`, a unix socket) is data, not
hardcoded logic.

enabled.description: When `false`, resolvers skip this entry without probing.

kind.description:
Network-path label driving priority + operator intent:
`lan_v4` | `lan_v6` | `tailscale_v4` | `tailscale_v6` | `fqdn` | `unix`.

kindLabel.description: Human display label for the path, when the mesh has one.

lastSeenAt.description: Epoch-millis this route was last observed reachable, when tracked.

path.description:
Export / share path on the server, for a route that addresses a mount
source rather than an HTTP endpoint. An NFS `host:/export` source folds
to `value = host`, `path = "/export"`; an SMB `//server/share` to
`value = server`, `path = "/share"`. `None` for endpoint/mesh routes,
which have no export path.

port.description:
Port, when applicable. `None` for schemeless mesh entries that carry the
port elsewhere, or for unix sockets.

register.description:
Desired-state intent: when `true`, orca should *realize* this route in the
world via the route-realization capability — fanning it out to every
registered realizer that handles its kind (an `fqdn` to Caddy + AdGuard +
Tailscale DNS; an ip/address to an OPNsense static route). A descriptive
route (a learned peer/topology address) leaves this `false` and is never
registered; only a route a consumer explicitly asks to register sets it.

scheme.description:
Transport scheme: `http` | `https` | `ws` | `wss` | `unix` | … .
`None` for mesh peers (dialed by `value:port`, no URL scheme).

value.description:
The BARE host / IP (or filesystem path when `kind`/`scheme` = `unix`).
Never a full URL — no scheme, no port.

Routes.description:
An ordered, priority-ranked set of reachability [`Route`]s for one
addressable thing.

This is the first-class collection the "no scalar URL — one ordered
`routes[]`" rule is built on: index 0 is the primary/base, the rest are
alternates in descending priority, and a consumer walks them in order until
one answers. The ordering-is-priority invariant, dedup, and the primary /
enabled accessors live HERE (as methods) instead of being re-implemented at
every call site over a bare `Vec<Route>`.

`#[serde(transparent)]` so it is wire- and column-identical to the
`Vec<Route>` it replaces (a bare JSON array) — no migration of stored rows.
Deref to `[Route]` gives every slice method (`iter`, `first`, `is_empty`,
`len`, `contains`) for free, and deref coercion lets a `&Routes` pass
wherever a `&[Route]` is expected (e.g. the plugin-toolkit resolver).

Runtime.description:
What actually executes a workload. Orthogonal to [`TargetKind`] (the
management surface) and to the host. This is the axis the migration engine's
per-runtime translators key on.

oneOf.description: Docker engine.
Podman engine (rootful or rootless).
System container (Proxmox `pct` LXC, …).
Full virtual machine (Proxmox `qm`, libvirt, …).

RuntimeKind.description:
Which container runtime backs an adapter / container row.

`RuntimeKind` is the single discriminator the reconciler keys on when it
picks a remediation primitive (e.g. `docker start` vs `pct start` vs
`machinectl start`). Adding a new runtime in the future means adding a
variant here, implementing [`RuntimeAdapter`] for it, and teaching
[`detect_available_runtimes`] to probe for it.

oneOf.description: Docker Engine / Moby (CLI today, Engine API later).
Proxmox / mainline LXC (`pct` / `lxc-ls`).
Podman (rootless or rootful).
systemd-nspawn (`machinectl`).

ScheduleCreateAction.description:
The `schedule.create` action. Only `run` today; the discriminant keeps the
surface six-verb-uniform.

oneOf.description: Invoke the row's job immediately, out-of-band from the loop.

ScheduleDetailView.description:
Which facet `schedule.detail` reports. `status` (per-job last-run history) is
the only view today; more fold in here as the enum grows.

isReplica.description: True if this is a replica from another owner.

name.description: Row name (the `name` column in config_rows).

nextRun.description: Next firing time (RFC3339, UTC) if the cron parses, else null.

SchemaColumn.description:
One column entry within `tabs[*].columns[tableName]`. Field names match
the HTTP `/api/schema` payload, camelCase like the rest of the surface
(`fkTarget`).

SchemaDomain.description: Domain grouping (loaded from each schema DB's `domainsFile` JSON).

errors.description: One human-readable message per schema violation.

backend.description:
Backend kind. `"inline"` stores the value in the encrypted DB; any other
kind (e.g. `"onepassword"`, `"bitwarden"`, `"vault"`) is resolved at read
time by the matching registered `secrets_backend` plugin.

SeriesRef.description:
A series/sequence position, tying a unit to the cross-format reading-order
convergence (e.g. Stormlight #1). Kept generic across media types.

ServedByEntry.description:
One server for a media type, with the reachable URL and (when `--user` was
given) that user's orca-managed credentials for device setup.

credentials.description:
Per-user credentials, resolved when `--user` was given and the backend
supports the `credentials` capability.

error.description: Non-fatal per-backend resolution error, if url/credentials couldn't resolve.

url.description: Reachable URL(s), resolved when the backend supports the `url` capability.

ServiceCapability.description:
The lifecycle operations a backend advertises it supports. Consumers branch
on capability before invoking. `Deploy` means the backend can produce a
[`WorkloadSpec`] (i.e. it runs as a container/VM via a deploy target);
device/host-only services (mikrotik, a host UPS daemon) omit it.

oneOf.description: Build the backend's `WorkloadSpec` and place it on a deploy target.
Snapshot a service instance's config/data into a restorable artifact.

ServiceDetailView.description:
Which facet `service.detail` reports. `status` (health/diagnostics) is the
first; more views fold in here as the enum grows.

ServiceHealthRow.description: One backend's projected health in the fleet aggregate.

instance.description:
Which registered instance this row reports on. `None` when the provider
has no registered instance — the row is then a statement about the
REGISTRY, not about the software's health (#615).

ServiceInfo.description:
Typed, plugin-specific `service.status` detail.

HARD RULE: no opaque JSON anywhere — every plugin's rich data is modeled as a
concrete typed variant here, owned centrally, so the full schema is always
known. A variant is added as each rich plugin (jellyfin/plex media,
homeassistant entities, arr indexers, …) is converted to the single surface.
`None` is the default for backends that report only health.

oneOf.description: Backend reported only health — no structured detail.

ServicePrimitive.description:
A typed capability a service exposes from the core, declared at
registration. "Primitives from core" — the generic building blocks core
owns, never opaque JSON.

oneOf.description: A reachable HTTP(S) API surface. `path` e.g. `"/api/v3"`.
A webhook/callback the service can emit.
A metrics endpoint (prometheus etc). `path` e.g. `"/metrics"`.
A health/readiness probe. `path` e.g. `"/ping"`.

ServiceProvider.description: Descriptor row for `service.list` / topology — a backend's own self-report.

runtimes.description: Runtimes this software can be placed on (via a matching deploy target).

ServiceRegistration.description:
One service identity a plugin registers at runtime, bound to an endpoint.

This is a wire + FFI shape (crosses the JSON proxy and, later, gossip) — keep
it additive: every non-essential field is `#[serde(default, …)]` so an older
peer's payload still deserializes.

host.description:
Host or IP the service is reached at. Correlated against a peer's
hostname and every known network address, the same resolution
[`crate::topology::TopologyClaim::runs_on`] gets.

port.description: Port the service listens on — the join key against a claim's endpoints.

provider.description: Provider that registered this (registry key component + display).

role.description:
Logical role/type, e.g. `"sonarr"`, `"adguard"`. A free string owned by
the plugin; core does not enumerate roles.

oneOf.description: Apply service-specific configuration to an instance idempotently.
Restore a service instance from a backup artifact path.

ShareRow.description:
A share/volume tagged with the backend that exposes it. Flat projection of
[`plugin_toolkit::storage::Share`] so consumers don't depend on the domain type.

configuredSources.description:
Configured ordered sources (primary → failover) for this share's `target`,
joined from the declarative `managed_mounts` store. `source` above is the
live/active source the backend reports; this is the authored failover
order. Empty when no managed mount declares this target.

SkipLabelReason.description:
Which label triggered a skip. Closed — there are exactly two label
gates in C3.

oneOf.description: `orca.skip=true` — operator escape hatch, never touch.
`orca.heal=manual` — notify-only, never act.

Source.description: One way a unit is served: by which server/share, over which method, at what URL.

by.description: The server app name (`plex`) or storage backend name (`smb`) doing the source.

SourceDismissResult.description: Outcome of pushing a dismiss back to the originating external source.

error.description: Failure detail when `ok == false`. The local dismiss still stands.

ok.description: Whether the source acknowledged the dismiss.

source.description: The source the dismiss was routed to.

cleared.description: Keys auto-dismissed because the source no longer reports them.

error.description: Set when the source's poll failed; its rows were left untouched.

oneOf.description: Streamed/transcoded by a media-server app (Plex/Jellyfin/Navidrome/ABS/…).

Served as a raw file over a storage protocol (SMB/NFS) — the file share is
itself a way this unit is served.

SourceProbe.description:
Which transport-liveness probe a source election runs against a candidate
source. [`Auto`](Self::Auto) resolves to [`Nfs`](Self::Nfs) for NFS
filesystem types (an RPC NULL that a *hung* nfsd will not answer even when
TCP is up) and [`Tcp`](Self::Tcp) otherwise (a bare TCP connect).

oneOf.description: A bare TCP connect to the source's transport port.

An RPC NULL to the NFS program — returns down when TCP is up but nfsd
does not answer, so election will not fail back onto a hung primary.

Resolve per filesystem type: [`Nfs`](Self::Nfs) for `nfs*`, else
[`Tcp`](Self::Tcp).

SpecDetailFormat.description:
Which spec surface `spec.detail` reports. `openapi` (default) dumps orca's
own OpenAPI JSON; `graphql` parses a registered `<repo>.graphql` SDL.

spec.description: Orca's own OpenAPI JSON document, pretty-printed.

SpecFormat.description:
Which spec surface `spec.update` mutates. `openapi` (default) drives the
registry-backed `action`s; `graphql` runs the Shopify GraphQL proxy.

oneOf.description: Re-fetch a previously-registered spec from its stored URL.
Connect to an MCP server and upsert every advertised repo.

StartFailure.description:
A `.start()` call that the adapter rejected. The row that triggered
the call is still in [`ReconcileOutput::rows`] with action
[`ReconcileAction::Started`] because the reconciler's *decision*
was to start it; the failure to actually start is recorded
separately so consumers can pair the two.

StartupOrdering.description:
Boot-time ordering declared by the runtime. Proxmox LXC `startup:
order=N,up=M,down=K` is the motivating shape (§2.1, §2.2 dep ordering);
docker has no equivalent and leaves every field `None`. Modeled as typed
fields rather than a raw string so the reconciler can compare across
runtimes without re-parsing.

downDelaySecs.description:
Seconds to wait after issuing shutdown before the host kills the CT.
Proxmox `down=<seconds>`.

upDelaySecs.description:
Seconds to wait after starting this CT before the host considers it
up enough to start the next ordered peer. Proxmox `up=<seconds>`.

StorageCapability.description:
A capability a backend supports. Consumers check these before invoking an
operation so an unsupported call fails fast rather than at the transport.

oneOf.description: Enumerate the shares/volumes this backend exposes.

Enumerate the exports this host *serves* (NFS `/etc/exports`, SMB shares),
as distinct from what it mounts.

Author the exports this host serves — the write side of [`Exports`].
Separate from [`Create`]/[`Remove`] (which are share/volume *lifecycle*):
a backend can publish an export for a volume it did not create, and an
appliance backend can create volumes it cannot re-export.
Mount a share onto a target path on a host.
Unmount a previously-mounted share (incl. lazy/forced recovery).
Report capacity/usage for a volume.
Create a new share/volume.
Remove a share/volume.
Probe for and self-heal stale / vanished mounts (lazy-release + remount).

StorageDetailView.description:
The facet of a storage resource `storage.detail` reports. `usage` (capacity)
is the first; more views (e.g. `health`) fold in here as the enum grows.

StorageKind.description:
The flavour of storage a backend provides. Deliberately coarse — consumers
branch on capability, not kind. Kind exists for display + topology grouping.

oneOf.description: Network file share mounted over the network (NFS export, SMB/CIFS share).

Host-local / hypervisor-managed disk storage (Proxmox storage pools,
LVM, ZFS, directory). Has no network-share semantics of its own but can
be enumerated and have its usage reported via an API.
Object storage (S3-compatible). Reserved for future adapters.

StorageMountAction.description: The imperative mount actions, folded onto `storage.mount.update`.

oneOf.description: Render the declared `managed_mounts` into the autofs map and reload.

Release a mount: `--id <placement>` (backend and path come from the row,
run on its owner), or a raw `--provider` + `--target` on this host.
Self-heal stale autofs mounts across the declared network shares.

StorageMountEditOutput.description: The updated `mounts` placement returned by the CRUD branch.

changed.description:
Config files that changed this run (the drift set). Empty = host already
matched the declared store.

reloaded.description: Whether autofs was reloaded (only when something changed).

rendered.description: Number of enabled network-share mounts rendered into the autofs map.

triggered.description: Mountpoints accessed to force an immediate mount (when `trigger`).

userspaceMounted.description:
Userspace-process (object-store/FUSE) mounts brought up this run, via the
owning backend's helper process rather than autofs.

userspaceUnmounted.description: Userspace-process mounts torn down this run (disabled rows).

StorageProvider.description:
A storage provider as registered with orca: a named backend, its kind, and
the capabilities it advertises. This is the row `storage.list` surfaces and
the topology aggregator turns into nodes/edges.

endpoint.description:
Human-readable endpoint, e.g. `nfs://10.0.0.5:/export/pool`,
`smb://nas/media`, `proxmox:node/local-lvm`. Never contains secrets.

name.description: Unique provider name (matches [`StorageBackend::name`]).

StorageReport.description:
Storage footprint snapshot — surfaces orca.db and log-dir sizes so
operators can spot bloat. Per project_db_size_and_retention: orca.db
stays small, logs go to files with size+retention.

dbSizeBytes.description: Size of `orca.db` (including SQLite WAL/SHM if alongside) in bytes.

lastRetentionSweepAt.description:
UNIX epoch seconds of the last retention sweep. `None` until the
sweep job lands.

StorageShareAction.description: The coordinated source operations folded onto `storage.share.update`.

oneOf.description:
Hold a failover route (set `enabled = false`) so convergence fails every
client off it, then lazily release this host's placements of the share.

Return a held route (set `enabled = true`); convergence re-includes it and
fails back if the policy's `return_to_primary` is set.

Coordinated source reboot: drain the route → reboot the source host →
wait until its nfsd answers again (not just TCP) → resume.

held.description: Whether the route is currently held (drained).

route.description: The route `value` that was drained / resumed.

sourceHealthy.description:
`reboot_source` only: whether the source's nfsd answered again within the
wait budget before resume.

StorageShareRegisteredList.description: A page of canonical `shares` definitions read from the replicated table.

errors.description:
Per-backend enumeration errors (non-fatal), keyed by provider name, so a
single unreachable backend doesn't blank the whole listing.

allOf.description:
1-min load average normalised to a 0–100% scale. Empty series until
the history ring starts retaining a load field — `SystemHistoryPoint`
does not record it today, so the points vector is always empty here.

windowSecs.description:
Time span between earliest and latest sample (seconds). Zero when the
series has fewer than 2 points.

SystemCreateAction.description:
The `system.install` action. Only `install` today; the enum keeps the
six-verb `create{action=…}` shape and room to grow.

oneOf.description: Install orca on this host.
Uninstall orca from this host (binary, MCP, symlinks, supervisor unit).
Kill stale orca runtime processes so a binary swap is picked up.

SystemDetailView.description:
Which lean, read-only facet `system.detail` reports. All are cheap
(local DB / on-disk state only) and never dial. The fat host snapshot stays
on `system.info.detail`; the paginated log/metric streams stay on
`system.logs` / `system.history` — none of those fold in here. Host
liveness moved out to its own first-class verb `system.health`.

oneOf.description: The lean install/state/config snapshot (default).
The per-host capability registry (was `system.capability_list`).
Resolved retention policy (was `system.retention_get`/`retention_list`).

SystemHistoryPoint.description:
One sample in the per-host rolling history ring. Written every refresh
tick by the daemon, read back as `SystemInfoReport.history`.

fsTotalGb.description:
Capacity of the filesystem hosting `~/.orca`, in GiB. Sampled into the
ring so capacity can be judged by TREND rather than by a current-level
threshold — see [`utils::capacity_trend`]. Without a series there is
nothing to fit, and "85% and climbing fast" is indistinguishable from
"85% for two years".

fsUsedGb.description:
Used space on that filesystem, in GiB (`total - avail`). Stored as used
rather than avail so it shares the monotonic-growth orientation of every
other `*_used_*` field in this struct.

processRssMb.description:
RSS of this orca process at sample time, in MiB. Lets the history
ring carry the daemon's own memory footprint alongside host memory
so a leak in orca is distinguishable from host-wide pressure.

SystemInfoReport.description:
Cross-platform OS / hardware / process / network snapshot. Every field
is optional so the same shape works on macOS, Linux, and (eventually)
Windows — a collector failure leaves the field `None` rather than
breaking the whole report.

capabilityLabels.description:
Parallel-indexed human labels for `detected_capabilities`. Same
length and ordering as `detected_capabilities`; empty when that
vector is empty. Server-owned for the same reason as
`system_type_label`.

claims.description:
Things this host claims to host (VMs it runs, containers under its
docker socket, LXCs, etc.). Populated by colocated provider plugins
(proxmox, unraid, docker, ...). Each entry's `macs` is the join key
the inference layer matches against other peers' `interfaces[].mac`.
`TopologyClaim` lives in `contract` so plugins can emit it without
depending on `system`.

cluster.description:
Cluster this host belongs to, when it is a member of one (e.g. the
proxmox corosync `cluster_name` from `/etc/pve/corosync.conf`).
Self-reported and mesh-propagated, so ANY daemon can group peers by
cluster without the cluster's plugin loaded locally — the inventory
layer buckets by this in addition to the local `ClusterRoster`.
`None` for standalone hosts. NEVER set by user config.

cpuUsagePercent.description:
Aggregate CPU utilisation 0–100 %. Requires two sysinfo refreshes;
always `None` on the very first CLI snapshot.

detectedCapabilities.description:
Capabilities the detector observed on this host (e.g. `"docker"`,
`"vm-host"`, `"lxc-host"`, `"backup-target"`, `"gpu-nvidia"`).
Empty when none were detected. Compared against
`expected_capabilities(system_type)` (a static table in the
server crate) to produce anomaly badges in the UI.

distro.description: Linux distro long name (`Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS`). `None` on macOS.

dmiProduct.description: DMI product name (`Standard PC (i440FX + PIIX, 1996)`, ...). Linux-only.

gpus.description: GPUs detected on this host (NVIDIA via nvidia-smi; AMD via sysfs).

history.description:
Rolling time-series — last N samples from this host's history ring
(`~/.orca/history/system.jsonl`). Capped at ~720 points (≈1 h at the
5 s refresh cadence). Empty until the background refresher has
written at least one tick.

loadAvg1.description: Unix load averages (1/5/15 min). `None` on Windows.

loadPercent.description:
1-minute load average normalised against logical CPU count, expressed
as a percent 0–100. Computed server-side as
`min(100, load_avg_1 / cpu_logical * 100)`. `None` when either field
is missing or `cpu_logical == 0` (no load average on Windows).
Numerator: `load_avg_1`. Denominator: `cpu_logical`.

memPercent.description:
Memory usage as a percent 0–100. Computed server-side as
`min(100, mem_used_mb / mem_total_mb * 100)`. `None` when either
numerator or denominator is missing, or when `mem_total_mb == 0`.
Numerator: `mem_used_mb` (total − available). Denominator: `mem_total_mb`.

meshListening.description:
`true` when this host's mesh accept loop (plugin host, default
port 12002) currently holds a TCP listener. `false` when the
bind failed at startup, the host was stopped, or it has not yet
started. Surfaces silent mesh-port bind failures that previously
rendered a host as "healthy" in `system_detail` while it was
invisible to peers. See [[project-system-detail-hides-mesh-bind-failure]].

meshPort.description:
Port the mesh accept loop is configured to bind. Paired with
`mesh_listening` so operators can see *which* port is (or isn't)
open without cross-referencing config.

parentKind.description:
Kind of parent edge: `"hypervisor"` (VM under a host), `"host"`
(container under its docker host), or `None`.

parentPeerId.description:
Inferred parent in the physical/virtual/container hierarchy.
Set by the inference task (mac-match on peers' `claims`), never by
user config. `None` until a claim matches one of this host's
interface MACs.

selfSecure.description:
Tier-2 secrets-storage permission (`self_secure`) for this host.
`true` = this host is authorized to hold encrypted secrets replicated
from other mesh members. Surfaced in the host drawer as a SECURE
toggle, independent of cert trust.

snapshotAtUnix.description:
Wall-clock when this snapshot was collected. Cached snapshots may be
up to ~30s stale; consumers use this to decide whether to trust a
metric like load average.

systemType.description:
Canonical system-type tag for this host. Exactly one value per host.
Drives expected-capability lookup and service-discovery class
selection. Values: `"unraid"`, `"proxmox-ve"`,
`"proxmox-backup-server"`, `"macos"`, `"debian"`, `"alpine"`,
`"nixos"`, `"truenas-scale"`, `"truenas-core"`, `"linux"` (fallback).
`None` only when the detector failed to run.

systemTypeLabel.description:
Human-readable label for `system_type` (e.g. `"Proxmox VE"` for
`"proxmox-ve"`). Server-owned so every surface renders identical text
without re-implementing the switch per client. `None` when
`system_type` is also `None`; unknown tags pass through verbatim.

topProcesses.description:
Top processes by CPU usage at snapshot time. Capped at 10 entries
(drawer renders them as a click-to-histogram table; widening the
list is cheap server-side but wastes wire bytes the UI can't
usefully render). Empty when sysinfo failed to enumerate.

virtualization.description:
Hypervisor / container kind: `kvm`, `qemu`, `vmware`, `lxc`,
`docker`, `none`, etc. Linux-only — read from `/sys/class/dmi/id/`
+ `/proc/1/cgroup`. macOS reports `None`.

channel.description:
Release channel marker (`stable` | `beta`). `None` when no channel
marker has been written. (Legacy `rc`/`prerelease` markers read as
`beta`; a legacy `dev` marker reads as `stable`.)

channels.description:
Every addressing channel for this host (LAN, Tailscale, manual
overrides, etc.). Was `system.host.detail.channels`.

allOf.description:
Runtime snapshot of the orca daemon: running / pid / port /
uptime_seconds. Was `system.daemon.status`. The `mode` and
`version` of the running daemon are sourced into the parent
fields above.

diagnostic.description:
Doctor entries (ok/warn/error) covering vault, agents, logs dir,
memory root, and auth config. Was a standalone `system.diagnostic`
tool; folded in here per the flat-namespace consolidation.

displayName.description:
Operator-visible host name (from the `display_name` addressing
channel, falling back to OS `hostname`).

frontend.description: "embedded" when this binary was built with the `ui` feature on, "disabled" otherwise.

mode.description:
Daemon operating mode: "daemon" | "parked" | "dev". `None` when the
state file is absent (binary not running as the registered daemon).

pinnedTo.description: Active version pin if any (`orca update --pin`).

allOf.description: orca.db + logs dir footprint. Used by UI host drawer + alerts.

target.description: Build target triple of this binary (e.g. `aarch64-apple-darwin`).

allOf.description:
